quote: Of the three stanzas in the Anushṭubh metre which are incised in ll. 23-28 and below the alphabet on the left hand side, the first dedicates the Varna-nāgakṛipānikā, i.e., the alphabetical snake-scimitar, to Udayāditya: and the second stanza states that this sword of kings Udayāditya and Naravarman, the worshippers of Śiva, was ready equally for the protection of the (four) Varṇas (classes of society) and of the Varṇas (alphabet), (by encouraging learning), with a pun on the word Varṇa. The third and the last of these stanzas purports to state that this serpentine sword of king Udayāditya, intended for the protection of letters (learning) and social classes has been set up as a badge for the poets and kings (rulers). It also says that the string of (poetic) gems was composed by “the friend of the talented poets” (sukavibandhunā), which, as Sastri rightly pointed out, presumably refers to king Naravarman himself, who appears to have composed the prāsasti.² Thus the drift of all these three verses taken together goes to show, as already indicated by Sastri, that the prāsasti was incised by Naravarman himself, during his reign, to commemorate the restoration of a temple of Śiva (the Mahākāla temple itself where the stone was found),³ and also that he associated his father’s name with his own as an expression of honour and filial love.

book_title: A Serpentine Scimitar of Letters (the varṇanāgakṛpāṇikā inscription at Udaypur) — Singh, A.
quote: The centrepiece of the inscription is the diagram containing individual letters within separate compartments (Fig. 3), which graphically visualise all the sounds of the Sanskrit alphabet as well as the grammatical terminations of nouns and verbs. Read in a vertical sequence from top to bottom, its geometrical “head” has 14 vowels (svara) ordered in short and long pairs, from the simple (a, ā > i, ̄ > u, ̄ > r, ̄ > l, ̄) to the complex (ē, ai) and compound (ō, au). The tubular “body” below carries a series of consonants, from the 4 semivowels (antahstha) in its neck to the 5 classes of stops (sparsha) in the rhomboidal knot of its torso, and continuing with the 3 voiceless sibilants (ūshman) in its right leg. This series starts and ends with the voiced aspirate ha, occur-ring once before the semivowels and again after the sibilants, in conformity with the classical arrangement of the alphabet given in the Śivasūtras of Pāṇini’s Aṣṭādhyāyī. The horizontal base of the diagram has 3 aspirates, the labial upadhmānīya, guttural jihvāmūlīya and final visarga, but not the nasal anusvāra, which usually counts among the 4 dependent sounds (ayogaṇāha). The left leg contains the characters ra, ya, u, although it is unclear why they are repeated. The tail-end of the diagram displays grammatical endings arranged in triads in the rise and fall of a vertical loop. The former has 21 terminations for nouns of all 7 classes, and the latter, 18 terminations for verbs in present tense in both active (paramaipada) and middle (āmamepada) voice.

quote: What this shows is that the serpentine graph was not so much an educational tool devised to school young boys in Sanskrit, as scholars have routinely remarked (Trivedi 1978, 88-89; Pollock 2006, 177). Rather it was a complex device pressed into service of the Paramāra kings who owed their allegiance to the cosmic overlord Śiva, praised in the Ujjain inscription as a personification of language itself (Salomon 1982, 556-557). This is perhaps why a copy of the remarkable composition was inscribed at the leading Śiva temples of the Paramāra kingdom—at Ujjain the nerve centre of Malwa but also at Udaypur, a town whose temple and tank were founded and named after king Udayāditya in 1080. The grammatical inscription from Udaypur, together with those from Ujjain, Dhar, and Un, thus, forms an important addition to the corpus of “serpentine scimitars of letters” attributed to Udayāditya and dateable to the last decade of the 11th century.

quote: As regards Navasâhasânka-carita, we have also sufficient reason to believe that it represents a solid historical fact in the garb of a romantic story. भावप्रकाश और रुचिवनिश्चय (माधवकृत) में उसे आयुवंदलेखक वताया गया है । केशवार्क ने भोज को ज्योतिर्यन्थ का रचयिता बताया । क्षीरस्वामी, सायण और महीप ने उसे वैयाकरण तथा … कोपकार वताया है। कवि चित्रप, विनायक शंकर सरस्वती, कुटुम्बदुहितू आदि ने भोज की काव्यक्षमता की प्रशंसा की है। शब्दसाप्राज्यम् मृत्य मे भोज्याकरण के अनुसार शब्दसिद्धि की गयी है। कार्ययेम ने शाकुन्तल-टीका में भोज को भरत के समान नाट्यवेता वताया है -
*Gloss [my translation]:* Bhavaprakasha and Ruchiviniscaya call him an Ayurveda author; Keshavarka an astronomy author; Kshirasvamin, Sayana and Mahipa a grammarian and lexicographer; poets praise his poetic ability; Shabdasamrajya is composed on Bhoja's grammar; Karyayem in the Shakuntala commentary calls Bhoja a knower of drama like Bharata.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
सुप्रसिद्ध टीकाकार मल्लनाथ ने भोज का कई सन्दर्भों में उल्लेख किया है । यथा अथशास्त्र, व्याकरण, कोप, काव्यशास्त्र, राजमृगांक (ज्योतिपु), चारुचर्यादि आचारप्रन्थ इत्यादि भोजकृतियों के उद्दरण दिये हैं । रामचन्द्र युधेन्द्र ने तो भोज को धनपाल के समान “निश्णेपवाङ्मयविद्” ही कहा है । इससे स्पष्ट है कि राजा भोज की विविध विपयक अनेक प्रामाणिक प्रन्थों के रचयिता के रूप में ख्याति थी । प्रभावकचरित में भोजकृत प्रन्थों के विभिन्न विषयों की एकत्र सूची ही दी थी जो तव शाला में पढ़ाये भी जाते थे । यथा - भोजव्याकरण, शब्द-अलंकारशास्त्र, तर्कशास्त्र, चिकित्साशास्त्र, राजसिद्धांत, रसशास्त्र, वासुशास्त्र, उदयशास्त्र, अंकशास्त्र, शकुनशास्त्र, अध्यात्मशास्त्र, स्वनशास्त्र, सामुद्रिकशास्त्र, निमित्ता-व्याख्यानशास्त्र, प्रशनचूढ़ामणि, अयःसद्भाविवृति, अर्थकाण्ड, मेघमाला इत्यादि ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Commentator Mallinatha cites Bhoja's works on political science, grammar, lexicon, poetics, astrology and conduct; Ramachandra Budhendra calls him like Dhanapala a master of all literature; Prabhavakacharita gives a list of Bhoja's works on many subjects, which were then taught in schools.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
भोज विविध विषयक इन प्रस्थों की रचना वड़ी शीघ्रता से कर लेता था। प्रवंध चिन्तामणि में भोज की इस विशेषता को रेखांकित किया गया है - जवाइन्थ नाना प्रवन्धः।
इसकी पुष्टि करते हुए सत्रहर्वीं शती का राजदूझामणि दीक्षित कहता है कि भोज ने एक रात में रामचरित रचा जिसे एक दिन में युद्धकांड रचकर चूझामणि पूरा कर रहा है
भोजेन रामचरितं प्रथितं निशयैकया ।
एकेन पूरयत्थना श्रीचूझामणि दीक्षितः ।।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Bhoja could compose works on diverse subjects very quickly; Prabandhachintamani underlines this; a 17th-century writer, Chudamani Dikshita, says Bhoja composed the Ramacharita in a single night, which Chudamani completes with the Yuddhakanda in one day.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
जयसिंह सिद्धराज का सभाकवि भी कहता है कि उसने एक दिन में महाकाव्य रच लिया था - एकाह निष्पत्र महाप्रवन्धः ।
इससे स्पष्ट है कि दक्ष रचयिता का भापा और शैली पर इतना अधिकार होता था कि वे एक दिन में भी पूरा काव्य रच सकते थे । राजा भोज ऐसा ही दक्ष रचनाकार था । अतः विभिन्न विषयक प्रस्थ एक साथ रच लेना भोज जैसे प्रतिभाशाली के लिए असंभव नहीं था । भोज के वंशज अजुनवर्मा सहित कितने ही अन्य प्रस्थकारों ने भी भोजदेव की असामान्य प्रतिभा की पुष्टि की है ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Jayasimha Siddharaja's court poet also says he composed a mahakavya in one day; skilled composers could write a whole poem in a day; Raja Bhoja was such a composer, so composing works on various subjects together was not impossible for him; others including his descendant Arjunavarman confirm Bhojadeva's talent.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
भोज के नाम से झात विभिन्न प्रस्थी की सूची इस प्रकार है -
1. साहित्य -
(1) घम्पूरागयण, (2) शुंगारमंजरीकथा, (3) अविनिकुमशत, (4) सुभाषितप्रवन्ध, (5) वार्देवीस्टुलि, (6) विद्याचिनोद, (7) शालिकथा, (8) महाकाली विजय।

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
राजा भोज की विविध विषयक रचनाओं को परवर्ती ग्रन्थकार प्रमाण मानकर उब्ज्त करते रहे। फिर चाहे वह साहित्यशास्त्र का सरस्वतीकण्ठाभरण हो अथवा शूंगारप्रकाश हो, धर्मशास्त्र हो अथवा ज्योतिपूर हो, वैद्यक हो अथवा जीवनचर्यां की चारचर्यां। शैव दर्शन हो अथवा व्याकरण, कोष हो अथवा नीति या अर्थशास्त्र, संगीत हो अथवा नाटक । स्पष्ट ही भोज को भारतीय विद्धत्समाज विशेष मान निरन्तर देता आ रहा है ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Later authors kept quoting Bhoja's works as authority, whether poetics, dharmashastra, astrology, medicine, Shaiva philosophy, grammar, lexicon, polity, music or drama; clearly Indian scholars have continually given Bhoja special regard.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
भोज ने वागदेवी की सुवित में पूरा काव्य ही नहीं रचा, अपितु सरस्वतीकणठाभरण, शूगारमंजरी सहित कितनी ही कृतिया में भी उसका नमन किया गया। यही नहीं 1034 ई. में भोज ने वागदेवी की मनोहर प्रतिमा भी बनवायी।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Bhoja not only wrote a whole poem in praise of Vagdevi; she is also saluted in Sarasvatikanthabharana, Shringaramanjari and other works; in 1034 CE Bhoja had a charming image of Vagdevi made.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
काव्यशास्त्र का सरस्वतीकण्ठाभरण विद्वज्जगत् में अलंकारम्ब्ध के रूप में वड़ा लोकप्रिय हुआ। इसकी भी अनेक टीकाएँ रची गयीं जिनमें से कुछ प्रकाशित हैं। व्याकरण के सरस्वतीकण्ठाभरण की भी टीकाएँ रची गयीं। इसी प्रकार शैवदर्शन के तत्त्वप्रकाश की भी टीकाएँ रची गयीं। भोज ने भी कुछ पुस्तकों की टीकाएँ की थीं। यथा - योगसूत्र टीका, अमरव्याख्या, मनुभाथ्य इत्यादि ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* The Sarasvatikanthabharana on poetics became popular as an alamkara text and many commentaries were written, some published; also on the grammar and on the Shaiva-philosophy Tattvaprakasha; Bhoja himself wrote commentaries, e.g. on the Yogasutra, Amara and Manu.

book_title: भोजदेव (Bhojadeva)
quote:
भोज का संकलित सुभापितप्रवन्ध 255 विभिन्न विपयक संस्कृत श्लोकों का प्रथम सुभापित संग्रह है । शेप संग्रह वाद में संकलित हुए हैं । अतः लघु होने पर भी इसका ऐतिहासिक महत्व है । क्योंकि इससे ही संस्कृत सुभापित-संकलन-धारा का प्रवर्तन होता है ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* Bhoja's compiled Subhashitaprabandha is the first subhashita collection of 255 Sanskrit verses on varied subjects; the rest came later; though short it has historical importance, since it began the Sanskrit subhashita-collection stream.

quote:
भोज विरचित नाममालिका नामक एक शब्दकोप प्रकाशित है । इसमें कई अल्पज्ञात शब्दाथों को प्रकट किया गया है ।
*Gloss [my translation]:* A dictionary composed by Bhoja called Nammalika is published; it reveals several little-known word meanings.

quote:
राजा भोज ने धारा
में सरस्वतीकृष्ठभरण नामक एक शाला का निर्माण करवाया था जो वात्स्यायन के कामसूत्र

एक केन्द्र उज्जैन में भी था।

वादेवी की प्रतिमा को पहले वनाकर, बुद्धि प्राप्त हो, ऐसी ठचि सम्पत्र (मनोहर) और

quote:
यहाँ तक कि नितान्त शुष्क शासकीय आदेश के ताम्रप्रो में भी राजा भोज ने काव्यात्मकता पर ऑच नहीं आने दी -
जयति व्योमकेशोसौ यः सर्गाय विभर्ति ताम् ।
ऐन्दवीं शिरसा लेखां जगद्वीजांकुराकृतिम् ।।
तत्पन्तु वः स्मरारातेः कल्याणमनिशं जटाः ।
कल्पान्तसमयोहामतडिढलयपिड्गला: ।।

quote: The inscription at Sudi quoted in Chapter 2 relates how the general Nagadeva entrusted the building of his temple to a certain Shamka. quote: On one occasion, two learned men, from a foreign country, visited Naravarman's court at Dhârâ, and proposed to the assembled company some poetic riddles. Jinavallabha at once gave them the right solutions, and returned them to the king. Naravarman was highly pleased with him, and received him with great honour upon his visiting Dhârâ on a subsequent occasion.
